bug_semantics: Stored XSS (CWE-79) in FluentCMS page/site Head HTML. An authenticated admin uses Add Page (PageSettingsModal Meta tags tab, FormTextarea bound to Model.Head) or site SEO Head to persist arbitrary markup in the page/site Settings['Head'] dictionary. PageHead.razor then emits that value with @((MarkupString)GetSetting('Head')), which bypasses Blazor HTML encoding and injects the payload into every visitor's document <head>. The same first-write also interpolates unsanitized GoogleTagsId into generated <script> tags via GetGoogleTagsScript(). CVE text calls this reflected XSS in FluentCMS 1.2.3; the live sink is stored MarkupString rendering, and published tags are v0.0.1–v0.0.5 rather than 1.2.3, but the mechanism matches issue #2403 / the third-party PoC (admin Add Page → script tag → XSS).
flaw_origin: The unsafe render was first written in PR #2140 member 79045878d9ba6b25da32e42d6441ea9b7f5fd209 ('#2139 add PageHead component' by TheHadiAhmadi). That commit added PageHead.razor/.cs and wired <PageHead fluentcms /> into layout head templates. Immediate parent 6e72d68d43e6d476d9ef28063f097779471cbb4a has neither PageHead files nor GetSetting('Head') MarkupString. Head was already a stored SEO setting from #2131 (1d926bc, site create/update textarea only) with no page-head emitter. GitHub squash-merged the PR as a947884cd6c9a29d3d564fad5a427b8567effc1c onto origin/dev; the reconstructable first-write is the member commit, not the squash.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2025-67349 is a published MITRE CVE (not withdrawn/rejected) describing XSS via unsanitized Head input on Add Page. The matching code is PageHead rendering Settings['Head'] as MarkupString, which is stored XSS after the admin Head textarea is saved; Copilot's issue-linked PR retitled the same bug as stored XSS in PageHead. The smallest first-write of those lines is PR #2140 member 79045878, not squash a947884c. Parent 6e72d68d was checked directly: PageHead files and GetSetting('Head') are absent. The later Add Page modal Head field (fb0a10fd) and earlier site Head storage (1d926bc) are input/storage, not the emitter. potential_fix.approach: Sanitize Head HTML with an allowlist that permits only safe head elements (meta, link, style, noscript) and their expected attributes before MarkupString rendering, and reject GoogleTagsId values that are not ^[A-Za-z0-9\-]+$ before embedding them in generated script tags.
potential_fix.rationale: The XSS sink is Blazor MarkupString of attacker-controlled Head/GoogleTagsId. Allowlisting strips <script> and event-handler attributes from Head, and the GoogleTagsId regex stops quote/tag breakout in the gtag snippet, which is the same change Copilot drafted in PR #2408.
